newsitem.title: USA: Great Western agrees to be acquired by Washington Mutual.
newsitem.headline: Great Western agrees to be acquired by Washington Mutual.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp., attempting to fend off a hostile takeover bid by A.H. Ahmanson and Co., said Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Washington Mutual Savings Bank for $6.6 billion.
The latest agreement, in which shares of Great Western will be exchanged for shares in Washington Mutual, tops the existing $6.1 billion bid from Ahmanson.

In a joint statement, Great Western and Washington Mutual said the merger would rank Washington Mutual third in deposits in the state of California and give it an entry into the state of Florida, where Great Western had $7.1 billion in deposits at the end of 1996.
Great Western is based in Chatsworth, Calif., and Washington Mutual is based in Seattle, Wash.
Based on 1996 results, the combined companies would have assets of $87.4 billion and deposits of $52.7 billion, the companies said.
Under terms of the merger agreement, Great Western shareholders would receive 0.9 share of Washington mutual for each of their Great Western shares.
Great Western closed Wednesday at $45 a share on the New York Stock Exchange and Washington Mutual closed at $53.25 a share on Nasdaq.

Washington Mutual had been considered a possible rival bidder since Ahmanson made its unsolicited approach last month. The Washington thrift has been making acquisitions and has said it would like to expand in California.

But Ahmanson has not ruled out raising its bid, and industry analysts have said Ahmanson, the largest savings and loan institution in the nation, might become a takeover target itself if it fails in its bid for Great Western.

Ahmanson's offer, in which it would exchange 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share, was originally valued at $6.5 billion, but the value has slipped because Ahmanson's shares fell in subsequent days.
Ahmanson closed at $42 a share Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange.
